subject: Discovery recap — multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, routing)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Sanchez <nora.sanchez@fintechco.com>; FintechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, routing)

Hi Nora / team,

Great to meet this morning — thanks for walking us through the platform and the challenges you’re seeing. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the key points, success criteria, and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Quick recap (high level):
- Primary pain: inconsistent per-customer rate limiting and quota enforcement across your proxy layer. Several tenants are hitting usage spikes that cause noisy neighbors and drive up infra/overage costs.
- Goal: enforce per-tenant rate limits, quotas, and tiered routing to model variants (standard / premium) so you can guarantee SLAs for high-value customers while containing cost for lower tiers.
- Current stack: AWS EKS, in-house API gateway (custom), Redis for short-term KV caching, and a lightweight request broker. No centralized per-tenant billing metering yet.
- Success criteria (you called out):
  - Per-tenant rate limits + burst controls enforced at the routing layer
  - Per-tenant quotas and billing signals exported to billing system
  - Ability to route requests to different model tiers based on tenant config (and fall back automatically)
  - 99th-pctl latency for priority tenants < 300ms token emit for typical 512-token requests

Open questions / asks from Redwood:
1) Can you share an anonymized tenant qps distribution (for the top 50 tenants)? This will help us size pooling and batching strategies.
2) Do you have an internal definition for tiering (e.g., "standard" = up to 10 TPS, "premium" = 100 TPS)?
3) Any network diagram or details on the current proxy/gateway path (very helpful for our architecture team).

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep-dive next week (30-60m) with Rishi Malhotra (solutions engineering) to map integration points and sketch a POC.
- Redwood will provide a short SLA draft and a POC MAP (milestones, acceptance criteria).
- Procurement: align on timelines/contracting cadence — Nora, you mentioned an internal 60-day procurement window.

Attachments: Meeting_Notes_20260318.pdf (high-level notes), MAP.xlsx (POC milestone template).

If that all looks right I’ll schedule the technical session for next Wed/Thu and include Rishi.

Thanks again — appreciate the time.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0147
